key_insight: A unified analytical model links loss diagnosis to design rules for photoelectrochemical cells, covering both built-in junction and semiconductor-electrolyte junction architectures.
engineering_relevance: The framework turns experimental I-V curves into actionable bottleneck identification, helping engineers prioritize absorber choice, interfacial engineering, and nanostructuring for higher PEC efficiency.
method: Models ideal and real PEC behavior with a consistent set of physically meaningful parameters
Generates efficiency maps, current-voltage curves, and Sankey energy-flow diagrams
Fits experimental I-V data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms
evidence_signal: The model is validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, and compared across Si, perovskites, hematite, and BiVO4.
watch_item: Performance-guided design depends on the quality and comparability of fitted experimental I-V data, which may vary across device architectures and measurement conditions.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
